info.title: Sanity Context API
info.description: Build knowledge bases from your content (file uploads, website crawls, and Sanity datasets), then read, triage, and steer what they produce.

_rev.description: The document revision. It changes on every write.

_createdAt.description: When the document was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

_updatedAt.description: When the document was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

knowledgeBaseId.description: The ID (`kb…`) of the knowledge base this document belongs to.

schemaVersion.description: The version of the document shape. Currently `1`.

revisionId.description: The ID of the build that last wrote this entry's content. An unchanged entry keeps its earlier value across builds.

path.description: The entry's slash-delimited path, such as `docs/api/webhooks`. Order entries by `path` to get the knowledge base outline.

tldr.description: A summary of the entry. `scope` is what the entry covers, and `excludes` is what it does not cover. `neighbors` lists the paths of related entries. `centrality` is how important the entry is: `core`, `standard`, or `peripheral`.

body.description: The entry content in Markdown, with inline `[N]` citation markers. Absent when the entry has no content of its own, such as a `virtual` entry.

topicHeadings.description: The H2 and H3 heading titles in `body`. Absent when the entry has no `body`.

citations.description: The sources that back this entry, one item per source.

supports.description: Which facts in the entry body this source backs, in a short phrase.

spans.description: Line ranges in the source's distilled content that back those facts, with the quoted text.

sourceLineStart.description: First line of the range, counting from 1. Line numbers match `GET .../sources/{sourceId}/content`.

sourceLineEnd.description: Last line of the range, inclusive.

quote.description: The exact text of the line range in the source.

claim.description: The text in the entry body that this citation backs.

exact.description: The exact entry text the citation backs.

prefix.description: Text immediately before `exact`, to tell apart repeated phrases.

suffix.description: Text immediately after `exact`, to tell apart repeated phrases.

_key.description: A unique key for this item in the `citations` array.

filename.description: A display name for the cited source. Builds currently set it to the `sourceId`.

status.description: The entry state. Builds currently write only two values: `virtual` for an entry that groups child entries and has no `body`, and `filled` for an entry with a written `body`. The other values are reserved.

generatedAt.description: When the build that last wrote this entry's content ran, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

EntryDoc.description: A `sanity.context.entry` document: one entry in a knowledge base outline, stored in your organization's document store. No endpoint returns this document. Use this schema to type GROQ query results.

_updatedAt.description: When the document was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

knowledgeBaseId.description: The ID (`kb…`) of the knowledge base this document belongs to.

schemaVersion.description: The version of the document shape. Currently `1`. An instruction without the current version doesn't appear in lists and doesn't affect builds.

statement.description: The instruction, in plain language. Builds follow it over the raw sources.

scopeSources.description: The sources the instruction is tied to. The instruction affects the entries that cite these sources. The API always sets at least one source. When `null`, the instruction isn't tied to any source and doesn't affect builds.

_key.description: A unique key for this item in the array. It matches `sourceId`.

sourceId.description: The ID of the source the instruction is tied to.

contentHash.description: The source's content hash when the instruction was last checked against it. When the source content changes, the instruction is checked again.

status.description: The instruction state. `active` instructions apply to every build. `archived` instructions don't apply: a source changed and no longer supports the instruction. Editing an archived instruction makes it `active` again.

archivedAt.description: When the instruction was archived, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` while `active`.

archivedReason.description: Why the instruction was archived. `null` while `active`.

origin.description: Where the instruction came from. `conflict` means it was created when you resolved a conflict issue.

sourceIssueId.description: The `_id` of the conflict issue this instruction resolved. Reopening that issue deletes this instruction.

severity.description: How serious the issue is. `critical`: content is wrong or missing in a way that can mislead an agent. `suggestion`: a change that improves quality.

scopePath.description: Path of the entry the issue is about, or `*` when it applies to the whole knowledge base. For `add_entry`, the path of the proposed entry.

issue.description: What the problem is, in one or two sentences.

suggestedFix.description: What to do to fix the issue.

kind.description: The issue type. `conflict` means two or more positions disagree on the same fact, and you choose which one is correct.

claimKey.description: A key naming the disputed fact, such as `free_tier.request_limit`. It never includes the disputed value, so every side shares it.

claim.description: The position as a self-contained sentence. This is the option you choose from.

value.description: The disputed value on its own, such as `10,000/month`, without the sentence.

entryPaths.description: Paths of the entries that state this position.

sourceIds.description: IDs of the sources that directly back this position.

span.description: Where in a source this position was read.

sourceId.description: ID of the source the position was read from.

lineStart.description: First line of the range, counting from 1. Line numbers match `GET .../sources/{sourceId}/content`.

lineEnd.description: Last line of the range, inclusive.

authority.description: How much weight the sources behind this position carry. `primary`: your own content, such as uploaded files and pages on your own site. `secondary`: other sources. `community`: forums and Q&A sites.

items.description: One position in a conflict, and the entries and sources it comes from.

sides.description: The conflicting positions, at least two. To resolve the conflict, pass the index of one side as `resolution`.

suggested.description: Index in `sides` of the suggested side, when there is one. It is only a hint: nothing is chosen until you resolve the issue.

oneOf.description: A conflict: two or more positions disagree on the same fact, and you choose which one is correct.

severity.description: How serious the issue is. `critical`: content is wrong or missing in a way that can mislead an agent. `suggestion`: a change that improves quality.

scopePath.description: Path of the entry the issue is about, or `*` when it applies to the whole knowledge base. For `add_entry`, the path of the proposed entry.

issue.description: What the problem is, in one or two sentences.

suggestedFix.description: What to do to fix the issue.

kind.description: The issue type. `gap`: your sources cover material that entries leave out. `update_required`: an entry is out of date with its sources or contradicts an instruction, and needs a rewrite. `add_entry`: your sources cover a topic that no entry covers. `remove_entry`: an entry has lost its sources or its topic no longer applies. `split_entry`: an entry covers several distinct topics and should become child entries. `merge_entry`: an entry has too few sources to stand alone, so merge it into a nearby entry or keep it as it is.

citedSourceIds.description: IDs of the sources that led to the issue. For `add_entry`, the sources the new entry would cite.

claimKey.description: A key naming the specific finding, when the check that found it sets one.

involvedScopes.description: Paths of the entries the issue involves, when it spans more than one entry.

oneOf.description: Any issue that is not a conflict: missing or outdated content, or a suggested change to the outline.

content.description: What an issue found. The shape depends on `kind`.

fingerprint.description: An identity for the finding that doesn't depend on its wording. It determines the issue's `_id`, so a reworded finding updates the same issue.

revisionId.description: The ID of the build that filed this issue. `null` when the issue was filed outside a build, such as when removing a source leaves an entry without sources.

status.description: The issue status. `open` means it is waiting for triage.

IssueDoc.description: A `sanity.context.issue` document: a build finding waiting for triage, stored in your organization's document store. No endpoint returns this document. Use this schema to type GROQ query results and Sanity Function filters. To change an issue's status, use the issues endpoints. Only a `conflict` issue can have a non-null `resolution`.

_rev.description: The document revision. It changes on every write.

_createdAt.description: When the document was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

_updatedAt.description: When the document was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

schemaVersion.description: The version of the document shape. Currently `1`.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization that owns the conversation. Filter on it in every query, because the document store also holds documents from other features.

threadId.description: Your identifier for the conversation thread, unique within the organization. It is the `threadId` in the conversations endpoint path and determines the document `_id`.

metadata.description: Tags that describe the conversation, such as `mcpEndpoints`, `app`, and `environment`. Filter on them in GROQ queries. `null` until a save includes `metadata`.

startedAt.description: When the API received the first save for this thread, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

messagesUpdatedAt.description: When the conversation was last saved, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

role.description: Who sent the message. `user` is the person talking to the agent, `assistant` is the agent, `system` is a system prompt, and `tool` is a tool call or tool result.

content.description: The message text. `null` when the message has no text, such as a tool call.

toolName.description: The name of the tool for a `tool` message. `null` on other messages.

toolType.description: The kind of `tool` message. `call` is the agent calling the tool, and `result` is what the tool returned. `null` on other messages.

error.description: Why this step failed, including any stack trace. Set it on the tool result for a failed tool call, or on the assistant message for a turn that failed instead of answering. `null` when the step succeeded.

timestamp.description: When the API first received this message, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. The API sets it. Resending an unchanged message at the same position keeps its timestamp. `null` for messages recorded before timestamps existed.

items.description: One message in a conversation transcript, with the time the API received it.

messages.description: The conversation transcript, in order. Each save replaces it.

modelProvider.description: The provider of the model the agent used. `null` until a save includes `modelProvider`.

modelId.description: The ID of the model the agent used. `null` until a save includes `modelId`.

tokenUsage.description: The running total of token usage for the conversation. `null` until a save includes `tokenUsage`.

coreMetrics.description: The latest classification result. `null` until you record one.

successScore.description: How well the agent resolved the user's needs, from 1 to 10.

sentiment.description: The overall sentiment of the conversation.

contentGaps.description: Topics the agent couldn't answer because it lacked content.

classifiedAt.description: When the latest classification result was recorded, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. The API sets it. `null` until you record a result.

classificationError.description: Why your classifier couldn't classify the conversation. `null` when no failure is recorded. Recording a result clears it.

sharing.description: Your choice to share conversation telemetry with Sanity. `null` until a save includes `sharing`.

metrics.description: Whether to share classification metrics with Sanity: scores, sentiment, content gap counts, message counts and sizes, tool names, and model and token usage. Message content is not included.

conversations.description: Whether to share full conversation transcripts with Sanity. When `true`, the API also sets `metrics` to `true`.

contact.description: How the Sanity team can reach you about your agent, such as an email address or a Discord handle.

ConversationDoc.description: A `sanity.context.conversation` document: one agent conversation and its classification, stored in your organization's document store. No endpoint returns this document. Use this schema to type GROQ query results. To record conversations, use the conversations endpoints.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization that owns the MCP endpoint. Filter on it in every query, because the document store also holds documents from other features.

publicId.description: The MCP endpoint's public ID (`mcp…`). It is set once at creation, never changes, and determines the document `_id`.

title.description: The MCP endpoint's display name. You can change it at any time.

name.description: The MCP endpoint's name in its URL, in lowercase kebab case such as `my-endpoint`. It is unique within the organization and can't change after creation.

type.description: The source type. `knowledge-base` serves a whole knowledge base.

id.description: The knowledge base ID (`kb…`).

type.description: The source type. `dataset` serves documents from a Sanity dataset, limited by the MCP endpoint's `groqFilter` when set.

id.description: The dataset, as `<projectId>.<datasetName>`.

items.description: A content source that an MCP endpoint serves: a knowledge base or a Sanity dataset.

sources.description: The content sources the MCP endpoint serves. Each source appears once, and the order has no meaning.

instructions.description: Prompt text the MCP endpoint serves to connecting agents. `null` when unset.

groqFilter.description: A GROQ filter that limits what the MCP endpoint's `dataset` sources serve. It has no effect on `knowledge-base` sources. `null` when unset.

McpDoc.description: A `sanity.context.mcp` document: the configuration of one MCP endpoint, stored in your organization's document store. No endpoint returns this document. Use this schema to type GROQ query results and Sanity Function filters. Manage MCP endpoints in the Context dashboard.

get.description: Returns the knowledge bases you can access in the organization set by `organizationId`. Results are cursor-paginated.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` value from the previous page. Omit it to get the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The organization to list knowledge bases for.

id.description: The knowledge base's unique ID, a UUID. Accepted anywhere a `knowledgeBaseId` is expected.

publicId.description: The knowledge base ID to show users, such as `kb3do82whm`. Accepted anywhere a `knowledgeBaseId` is expected. Treat it as an opaque string.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization that owns the knowledge base.

description.description: A short description of what the knowledge base covers.

state.description: The knowledge base's build state. `created`: not built yet. `ready`: built, with no open issues. `review`: built, with open issues to review. A failed build doesn't change the state. `building`, `stale`, and `paused` aren't currently returned. To check for a running build, use `isBuilding`.

activeJobId.description: The job ID of the most recent build, or `null` if no build has started. Check its progress with `GET .../jobs/{jobId}`.

isBuilding.description: Whether a build is running now.

buildStageState.description: Progress of the most recent build, by stage. `null` until a build reports progress. It can briefly belong to an earlier build, so use it only when its `jobId` matches `activeJobId`.

jobId.description: The ID of the build job this progress belongs to.

id.description: The stage's ID. The values are listed in the order stages run.

status.description: The stage's status. `pending`: not started. `running`: in progress. `done`: finished. `failed`: the build ended before the stage finished.

units.description: The stage's progress counts. Absent when the stage hasn't reported counts.

unit.description: What `done` and `total` count: `sources`, `groups` of related content, `entries`, or `rounds` of final fixes. A `rounds` stage has no `total`.

done.description: How many units the stage has finished.

total.description: How many units the stage will process. Absent when `unit` is `rounds`.

stages.description: The build's stages and their progress. Stages that haven't reported yet can be missing.

lastCheckedAt.description: When a refresh last checked the knowledge base for changes, whether or not anything changed. `null` until the first refresh.

lastChangedAt.description: When the content last changed: the time of the most recent successful build. `null` if the knowledge base has never built.

hasPendingChanges.description: Whether sources were added, changed, or removed since the last successful build. Always `false` before the first build.

pendingChanges.description: Counts of sources added, changed, and removed since the last successful build. Only `GET .../knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}` computes it. `null` in list responses and before the first build.

added.description: Sources added since the last successful build, including sources no successful build has included yet.

changed.description: Sources whose content changed since the last successful build.

removed.description: Sources that recent refreshes no longer find.

pipelineOutdated.description: Whether Sanity Context has improved how it builds knowledge bases since the last successful build. Rebuild to apply the improvements. Always `false` before the first build.

rebuildRecommended.description: A recommendation to rebuild, because new or changed content doesn't fit the current outline. `null` when there's no recommendation. A refresh where the content fits again, a successful build, or adding or removing sources clears it.

reason.description: Why a rebuild is recommended, written to show to users.

hasWebSource.description: Whether the knowledge base has at least one website source.

hasDatasetSource.description: Whether the knowledge base has at least one Sanity dataset source.

sourceUsage.description: How many sources the knowledge base uses, and its source limit.

used.description: The number of sources counted toward the limit, including parts split from large sources.

limit.description: The maximum number of sources the knowledge base can have.

buildRestriction.description: Why a build request would be denied right now, or `null` if you can build. Only `GET .../knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}` checks it. List and create responses always return `null`.

code.description: A stable code for the restriction, such as `planLimitReached`.

message.description: A readable explanation that you can show to users.

refreshEnabled.description: Whether scheduled refresh is on. Only applies to knowledge bases with a website or dataset source.

refreshFrequency.description: How often scheduled refresh runs: `weekly` (the default) or `monthly`.

refreshNextRunAt.description: When the next scheduled refresh runs. `null` when scheduled refresh is off or not scheduled yet. Only `GET .../knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}` computes it, so list responses return `null`.

refreshInFlight.description: Whether a refresh is running now. While it's `true`, a new refresh request doesn't start another one. Only `GET .../knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}` computes it, so list responses return `false`.

openIssueCount.description: The number of open issues waiting for review. Always `0` before the first build.

instructionCount.description: The number of active instructions for the knowledge base.

createdBy.description: Who created the knowledge base. `null` if unknown.

id.description: The Sanity user ID, or `sanity-system` when Sanity Context made the change. `null` if unknown.

displayName.description: The user's name when the action happened. `null` if unknown. For the current name, look up the user by `id`.

createdAt.description: When the knowledge base was created.

updatedAt.description: When the knowledge base was last updated.

items.description: A knowledge base and its current state.

nextCursor.description: The cursor for the next page. Pass it as `cursor` to get more results. `null` when there are no more pages.

put.description:
Creates or updates the recorded conversation for one thread. `threadId` identifies the conversation within your organization, so saving with the same `threadId` updates the same conversation. Requires Context Editor access or higher.

Each save replaces the stored messages. `metadata`, `sharing`, and the model fields change only when you include them. `tokenUsage` is cumulative: send the usage for one generation call, and the API adds it to the conversation total. Usage is added only when the save changes the messages, so retries don't count it twice.

To report a failure, set `error` on the message where it happened: the tool result for a failed tool call, or the assistant message for a turn that failed instead of answering. The Insights dashboard highlights conversations with a failed turn and counts failed tool calls separately, because agents often recover from them.

The last write for a thread wins, so retries are safe. `sharing` records whether you share telemetry with Sanity: metrics only, or full transcripts.

toolName.description: The name of the tool for a `tool` message. `null` on other messages.

toolType.description: The kind of `tool` message. `call` is the agent calling the tool, and `result` is what the tool returned. `null` on other messages.

error.description: Why this step failed, including any stack trace. Set it on the tool result for a failed tool call, or on the assistant message for a turn that failed instead of answering. `null` when the step succeeded.

items.description: One message in a conversation transcript.

messages.description: The full transcript so far, in order. It replaces the stored messages.

modelProvider.description: The provider of the model the agent used. When absent, the stored value stays unchanged.

modelId.description: The ID of the model the agent used. When absent, the stored value stays unchanged.

tokenUsage.description: Token usage for one generation call. The API adds it to the conversation total, but only when this save changes the messages.

metadata.description: Up to 20 tags that describe the conversation. Well-known keys are `mcpEndpoints` (names of the MCP endpoints the conversation used), `app`, and `environment`. Add any other keys you need. Replaces the stored metadata. When absent, the stored value stays unchanged.

metrics.description: Whether to share classification metrics with Sanity: scores, sentiment, content gap counts, message counts and sizes, tool names, and model and token usage. Message content is not included.
